messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] another failure on develop
parts:
Ok. I found the reason it isn't working. For anyone that doesn't care about this stuff, you can check out now. It works fine under Windows.


We need to define a static pattern rule. The issue is that the target has no extension. For example, if the Stan file is normal.stan, then the make target in !win is normal.

The target we defined is:
.PRECIOUS: %.cpp %.o
%$(EXE): %.o bin/libstan.a
@echo ''
@echo '--- Linking C++ model ---'
$(LINK.c) -O$O $(OUTPUT_OPTION) $< $(LDLIBS)

Unfortunately, when $(EXE) is empty, this essentially matches every make target, so make chooses not to use it. It uses the default implicit target instead, which uses $(LINK.cxx), I think. I think by updating the make targets, I might be able to fix this once and for all.


Daniel

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] another failure on develop
parts:
Ben and Marcus, I just submitted a pull request that should fix the issue. Could one of you review this pull request?
https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/pull/140


For the makefile sent, replace
%$(EXE): %.o
with
$(patsubst %.stan,%,$(wildcard $(addsuffix .stan,$(MAKECMDGOALS)))) : %$(EXE): %.o

That should make it work. That's a static pattern rule. I've taken the goals, added .stan to the goals, searched for file existence, then stripped the .stan off. Those are the targets we are interested in.


Daniel

%$(EXE): %.o

$(patsubst %.stan,%,$(wildcard $(addsuffix .stan,$(MAKECMDGOALS)))) : %$(EXE): %.o
